family_history: Father: PKD with cerebral aneurysm (ruptured at age 52)

social_history.tobacco: Former smoker, 10 pack-years, quit 8 years ago

patient.chief_complaint: Sudden severe headache this morning while at work, brief loss of consciousness
patient.history_present_illness: Ms. Rodriguez is a 50-year-old woman with polycystic kidney disease and a strong family history of cerebral aneurysm who presents after sudden onset of the worst headache of her life at work this morning. She was at her desk when she experienced an instantaneous explosion of severe headache, 10/10, immediately followed by brief loss of consciousness lasting approximately 30-60 seconds. Coworkers witnessed her slump in her chair and called 911. By EMS arrival, she was awake but confused. On transport, she vomited twice. In the ED, she is now alert and fully oriented. She reports persistent headache 8/10 with neck stiffness. She has had intermittent headaches in the past, but nothing of this severity or character. She specifically notes she was placed on a surveillance MRA program 3 years ago after her father died from a ruptured aneurysm (PKD-associated), and her last MRA 18 months ago showed no aneurysm. She was due for repeat imaging in 6 months. She is extremely anxious about her diagnosis. She denies ongoing focal weakness, visual changes, or speech difficulty. PKD was diagnosed 12 years ago; her renal function has been stable.

output.wall_motion: Severe apical akinesis, basal hyperkinesis - classic Takotsubo
output.impression: 1. Moderate-to-severe apical ballooning pattern with severe apical akinesis and basal hyperkinesis; LVEF 38%. Findings are consistent with Takotsubo (stress) cardiomyopathy. 2. Mild mitral regurgitation from annular dilation. 3. No intracardiac thrombus. Cardiology consultation and repeat echocardiogram in 2–3 weeks recommended.
recommended_actions: Repeat echocardiogram in 2-3 weeks recommended; cardiology consultation suggested

quantitative_data.clinical_status: Patient with new bifrontal headache and mild confusion

recommended_actions: Daily TCD monitoring recommended; CT perfusion recommended if clinical deterioration

output.query: Polycystic kidney disease intracranial aneurysm prevalence screening

results.finding: Intracranial aneurysm prevalence in PKD 9-12% vs 2-3% general population
ADPKD screening with MRA recommended if family history of aneurysm or previous SAH
PKD aneurysms typically larger, multiple, and higher rupture risk

output.summary: Intracranial aneurysm prevalence in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease is approximately 9–12%, compared to 2–3% in the general population. MRA surveillance is recommended for PKD patients with a family history of SAH or aneurysm. Aneurysms in PKD patients may be multiple and may develop or grow between surveillance intervals. Clinical correlation recommended.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage from anterior communicating artery aneurysm in PKD patient (Hunt-Hess 3, Fisher 3)

differential.key_features: CTA shows saccular aneurysm; subarachnoid (not parenchymal) distribution; PKD-associated aneurysm confirmed
CT and CSF positive for SAH; LOC at onset

optimal_actions.action: Interpret labs - note hyponatremia and troponin elevation

optimal_actions.expected_finding: QTc 524 ms with U-waves - correct K, avoid QT drugs
8.4 mm AComA aneurysm; incidental left PComA 3.1 mm

optimal_actions.action: Start nimodipine, hold ramipril and furosemide
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Hold furosemide (CSW, volume depletion); hold ramipril (hypotension risk)

optimal_actions.action: Monitor and treat hyponatremia - cerebral salt wasting vs SIADH
optimal_actions.expected_finding: High urine Na confirms CSW - treat with IV saline (not fluid restriction)
Severe Takotsubo EF 38% - limits triple-H therapy options

critical_actions: CTA to identify AComA aneurysm - expedite treatment
Correct hyponatremia with IV saline (cerebral salt wasting - NOT fluid restriction)
Avoid QT-prolonging drugs given QTc 524 ms
ICU admission with continuous cardiac monitoring
Monitor for ICP elevation given hydrocephalus
contraindicated_actions: Do not restrict fluids for hyponatremia without distinguishing CSW from SIADH - fluid restriction in CSW worsens cerebral perfusion
Do not give QT-prolonging antiemetics (metoclopramide, haloperidol) with QTc 524 ms
Do not aggressively lower BP below 160 before aneurysm secured if vasospasm present
Do not administer furosemide (worsens CSW-related volume depletion)
key_reasoning_points: PKD is associated with a 4-5x increased risk of intracranial aneurysm; family history further compounds this risk
This patient had surveillance but the aneurysm developed between 18-month intervals, illustrating interval rupture risk in PKD
Hyponatremia in SAH must be distinguished between cerebral salt wasting (CSW, hypovolemic - treat with saline) and SIADH (euvolemic - treat with fluid restriction)
High urine sodium (>40 mEq/L) with volume depletion signs indicates CSW, not SIADH
QTc 524 ms with hypokalemia creates critical arrhythmia risk - Torsades de Pointes
Takotsubo cardiomyopathy with EF 38% limits aggressive triple-H therapy for vasospasm
Incidental PComA aneurysm (3.1 mm) discovered on CTA - PKD multiple aneurysm phenotype - plan treatment after acute phase

red_herrings.data_point: Troponin I 0.32 ng/mL elevation and BNP 286 pg/mL with QTc 524 ms on ECG
red_herrings.intended_effect: Marked troponin elevation and critically prolonged QTc may suggest acute coronary syndrome as the primary diagnosis or lead to cardiac catheterization, diverting focus from the SAH and delaying aneurysm treatment
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Neurogenic Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (confirmed by echo with EF 38%) caused the troponin elevation, BNP rise, and QTc prolongation via catecholamine surge from SAH. These are common SAH complications, not primary cardiac events. Cardiac catheterization is not indicated; priority is aneurysm treatment. QTc 524 ms requires avoidance of QT-prolonging drugs and monitoring, not cath lab.
